summary: Independent read-only hosted-agent planning audit of source a060ddd531753b3ed8bcd339ea8cc8a907ac6d7c and artifact digest cf9c1d1ce0c04793a293a38459e2567f528bb71eb89e3f8c7f5182638416fd17. One important contract gap remains: the new sync error contract does not preserve explicit wrong-owner 404 semantics. The proposal otherwise states current recipient-specific consent, separate sync/AI authority, owner/session-generation isolation, source-bounded payload-copy retention, export exclusions, purge of new stores and recoverable backups, fail-closed restore/revocation reconciliation, and content-free diagnostics. These are planned controls, not verified implementation. Existing pending owner/design/governance/boundary decisions remain pending; this audit introduces no additional product choice. This JSON is hosted-agent audit evidence, not a canonical planning gate pass: the six CLI reviewer executions produced zero reports after proxy CONNECT 403 failures and the formal campaign remains escalated. No implementation, build, repository mutation, or production verification was performed.

findings.description: The normative sync error table provides ACCESS_DENIED/403, but never specifies the accepted indistinguishable 404 behavior for a caller supplying another owner's scope, device, snapshot, or transaction-transfer identifier. Receipt lookup alone says it must not expose another owner's command existence; that does not define the other new resource paths or distinguish resource ownership failure from the advertised 403 policy error. A straightforward implementation of the listed authorization failure could therefore reveal that a foreign identifier exists instead of treating it as absent. This is an explicit contract omission, not evidence that any unimplemented endpoint currently leaks data.
evidence: docs/decisions/0001-vnext-modular-monolith-and-workflow-contracts.md:569-571: all reads, transitions, references, media and list queries are owner-scoped; wrong owner receives 404.
docs/auth.md:23: wrong-owner 404 rather than 403 prevents resource-existence probing.
specs/026-rust-core-sync/contracts/sync-v1.md:212-218: non-disclosure is stated for command lookup, while the general error table specifies ACCESS_DENIED/403 and has no owner-safe not-found mapping.
specs/026-rust-core-sync/contracts/sync-v1.md:113-121 and 232-242: new scope-selected device/snapshot/change and transaction-transfer/page paths require a shared ownership-error contract.
backend/app/modules/tasks/repository.py:748-766 and backend/tests/test_task_owner_isolation.py:51-55: the existing task lookup filters by owner and raises NotFoundError for another owner's task.
specs/026-rust-core-sync/quickstart.md:51: Q05 requires cross-owner IDs to reveal no content but does not assert missing-versus-foreign response equivalence.
findings.recommendation: Specify a single owner-safe resource-not-found response for unknown and foreign scope/device/snapshot/transfer IDs before any resource metadata is returned, preserving ADR-0001's 404 rule. Limit ACCESS_DENIED/403 to explicitly defined failures that do not disclose foreign-resource existence. Preserve command lookup's owner-scoped not_found semantics within an already-authorized scope. Add the unknown-versus-foreign response equivalence to the existing Q05/PR-30–33 authority checks; no new product decision or expanded feature is needed.
